Terminology management. The glossary is: Terminology management. The glossary is injected into translation prompts so established terms are used consistently.

Override any built-in AI prompt with you: Override any built-in AI prompt with your own prompt file. Paths are relative to the workspace root; leave a field empty to use the built-in prompt.
Translation pairs are the heart of mdait: Translation pairs are the heart of mdait: each pair maps a source directory to a target directory. Files under the source directory are translated to the same relative path under the target directory. Language codes are ISO 639-1, optionally with a region (e.g. 'ja', 'en', 'zh-CN'). Add one pair per target language. A per-pair 'copyAssets' override can be added directly in mdait.json.
The pivot language shared by the glossar: The pivot language shared by the glossary and the translation memory. Set it to the language your terminology is authored in — usually the source language of your documentation. Required.
Glob patterns for files and folders mdai: Glob patterns for files and folders mdait must never touch during sync or translation (e.g. '**/node_modules/**', '**/drafts/**'). One pattern per row.
Heading level at which documents are spl: Heading level at which documents are split into translation units. The default 3 starts a new unit at every '###' or shallower heading. Smaller values make larger units, larger values make finer units. 0 disables automatic marker insertion so you place '<!-- mdait -->' markers by hand. Can be overridden per document in its frontmatter.
Legacy switch for target units whose sou: Legacy switch for target units whose source unit was deleted. Prefer 'Orphan Target Policy', which supersedes it (true behaves like 'delete', false like 'verify'). Ignored when Orphan Target Policy is set.
What sync does with orphan target units: What sync does with orphan target units — translated sections whose source section no longer exists. 'delete': remove them automatically. 'verify': keep them flagged need:verify-deletion so a human confirms each removal. To keep target-only content permanently, make it an independent unit (a marker with a hash but no 'from'); to keep a unit while stopping downstream propagation, flag it need:isolate. Both are always preserved by sync regardless of this policy. Takes precedence over Auto Delete.
Automatically sync a file when it is sav: Automatically sync a file when it is saved. Only files that already contain mdait markers are synced, so unrelated files are never modified. Sync is deterministic and never calls AI.
Whether sync copies non-translated files: Whether sync copies non-translated files (images and other assets) from source to target directories. true copies everything that is not a translation target, false disables copying, or provide an extension whitelist such as [".png", ".jpg"]. Because the value can be a boolean or a list, edit this key directly in mdait.json.
Where unit markers live. 'embedded' (def: Where unit markers live. 'embedded' (default) keeps them as invisible HTML comments inside each document — self-contained and robust when files are copied or moved. 'external' stores them in .mdait/unit-state so documents stay completely clean; convert existing documents with the 'mdait: Externalize markers' / 'Embed markers' commands.
The AI backend used for translation and: The AI backend used for translation and terminology. 'vscode-lm' (default) uses the VS Code Language Model API — your GitHub Copilot subscription, no API key needed. 'openai' calls an OpenAI-compatible API configured below. 'ollama' uses a local Ollama server configured below. 'default' is a test-only mock provider that does not call an external LLM.
Vendor identifier for the VS Code Langua: Vendor identifier for the VS Code Language Model API, used with the 'vscode-lm' provider. Normally leave this as 'copilot'.
Model name used with the selected provid: Model name used with the selected provider. With 'vscode-lm' it must match a model your Copilot plan offers (e.g. 'gpt-4.1'); with 'openai' it is passed to the API as-is.
URL of your Ollama server. The default ': URL of your Ollama server. The default 'http://localhost:11434' works for a local installation. Only used when the provider is 'ollama'.
Ollama model used for translation (e.g. 'llama3', 'mistral'). Pull it first with 'ollama pull <model>'. Only used when the provider is 'ollama'.
Seconds to wait for the first response a: Seconds to wait for the first response and between streaming chunks before giving up. Increase for large models that load slowly. Only used when the provider is 'ollama'.
How long the model stays loaded in Ollam: How long the model stays loaded in Ollama's memory after a request, e.g. '10m' or '1h' (a plain number means seconds). Longer values avoid reload delays during a translation session. Leave empty to use the Ollama server default (5 minutes).
API key for the OpenAI-compatible endpoi: API key for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Strongly recommended: reference an environment variable with ${env:OPENAI_API_KEY} instead of pasting the key here — mdait.json is usually committed to git. Only used when the provider is 'openai'.
Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible API. C: Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible API. Change it to use a proxy or a compatible service. Only used when the provider is 'openai'.
Maximum tokens the model may generate pe: Maximum tokens the model may generate per response. Raise it if long units get truncated; lower it to cap cost. Only used when the provider is 'openai'.
Seconds to wait for an API response befo: Seconds to wait for an API response before the request fails. Only used when the provider is 'openai'.
Write AI call statistics (duration, toke: Write AI call statistics (duration, token counts) to .mdait/logs/ai-stats.log. Useful for tracking cost and performance; contains no document content.
Write full prompts and responses to .mda: Write full prompts and responses to .mdait/logs/ai-detailed.log. Helpful when investigating translation quality, but the log contains your document text — keep it off otherwise.
Keep fenced code blocks untouched during: Keep fenced code blocks untouched during translation. Turn this off only if you want comments and strings inside code examples translated too.
Frontmatter keys to translate (e.g. 'tit: Frontmatter keys to translate (e.g. 'title', 'description'). All other keys are copied verbatim. An empty list disables frontmatter translation.
How many neighboring units (before and a: How many neighboring units (before and after) are sent to the AI as reading context. More context improves consistency across section boundaries but increases token usage. 0 sends the unit alone.
How many times a failed unit translation: How many times a failed unit translation is retried before it is reported as an error (1-5).
Size limit in bytes for translating non-: Size limit in bytes for translating non-Markdown files. Larger files are skipped with a warning so a single huge file cannot cause runaway AI cost.
How many files are translated in paralle: How many files are translated in parallel during a directory translation (1-8; 1 = one at a time). Lower it if your AI provider rate-limits you; with 'vscode-lm' throughput depends on your Copilot quota.
Additional file extensions to translate: Additional file extensions to translate besides Markdown, e.g. '.txt' or '.csv'. These files are translated as a whole (no unit splitting) and tracked in .mdait/unit-state.
General cost guard for the maximum numbe: General cost guard for the maximum number of units processed in one pass over a single file. Applied per file by translation, AI translation review and AI align, so a directory run scales with the file count. When exceeded, translation and review keep the unit's need flag and process the rest on the next run, while AI align skips the file and keeps the position-based mapping. Set to 0 for no limit.
File name of the glossary inside the .md: File name of the glossary inside the .mdait folder. The extension decides the format: .csv or .yaml/.yml.
Master switch for the translation memory: Master switch for the translation memory. When enabled, confirmed translations can be committed to .mdait/translations.tmx and similar past translations are shown to the AI as reference while translating.
Maximum number of similar past translati: Maximum number of similar past translations attached to a translation prompt. More references can improve consistency but increase token usage.
How many focused retries are attempted w: How many focused retries are attempted when a TM commit fails its alignment guard (1-5).
Minimum number of characters (after norm: Minimum number of characters (after normalization) a line needs to be used as a TM search query. Filters out noise from short fragments such as table cells.
Custom prompt file for initial unit tran: Custom prompt file for initial unit translation.
Custom prompt file for diff-aware revisi: Custom prompt file for diff-aware revision — updating an existing translation from a source diff while preserving manual edits.
Custom prompt file for glossary term det: Custom prompt file for glossary term detection.
Custom prompt file for extracting term t: Custom prompt file for extracting term translations from already-translated documents.
Custom prompt file for translating gloss: Custom prompt file for translating glossary terms.
Custom prompt file for TM sentence align: Custom prompt file for TM sentence alignment.
Custom prompt file for single-pair AI tr: Custom prompt file for single-pair AI translation review (used when the review batch size is 1).
Custom prompt file for batched AI transl: Custom prompt file for batched AI translation review (used when the review batch size is 2 or more).
Custom prompt file for the AI align step: Custom prompt file for the AI align step (differential review of the unit mapping during adopt).
Let the AI review clear need:review auto: Let the AI review clear need:review automatically for pairs it judges to be faithful, complete translations with high confidence. Turn off for report-only mode where no markers are changed.
How many pairs are verified per AI call. 1 uses the single-pair prompt; larger batches reduce the number of calls and the cost of a run.
Rows with empty fields are not saved unt: Rows with empty fields are not saved until all fields are filled.
